text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Faced with an exodus of fleeing Albanians, Italy said that Europe was committed to efforts to rebuild the Balkan state and urged would-be refugees to remain at home. Prime Minister Romano Prodi went visit the southern port of Brindisi and told reporters, "the crisis will not be resolved by fleeing but by the rebuilding of Albania. Europe will provide the material conditions for this to happen" (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party's president Armando Cossutta said "it would be better" not to apply any mini-budget this coming spring and repeated his party's firm opposition to cuts in welfare and pensions spending or new taxes (all).
* Opposition party Freedom Alliance said Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi ought to admit that the mini-budget will amount to some 15 trillion lire (all).

* In an interview, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said that it might be necessary to touch severance pays (Tfr) in public companies. Treu added that industrialists' should do their share and that he agreed with Treasury Minister Ciampi's cautious position about the actual size of the mini-budget (La Repubblica).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
